The stolen information includes card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV or CVC security codes. Cleverbridge’s public update does not list those fields or say whether the same details were exposed for every affected customer. The company began notifying affected individuals on November 20, 2026. According to Cleverbridge’s incident update , the company detected unauthorized activity on November 4 and temporarily took affected systems offline to contain it. items.title: Are VPNs Safe? What Has Gone Wrong, What Has Held Up
items.summary: A VPN from a company with a checkable record is safe to use, and legal in most countries. The risk is the company itself, because it sees the traffic you’re hiding from everyone else. That’s the trade at the heart of every VPN. Your internet provider, the café Wi-Fi and the sites you visit see less, and one company sees more. Most of the time that company keeps its word. Sometimes it hasn’t, and both kinds of story are on the public record: court files, police searches, leaked databases, audit reports. They tell you more than any “military-grade encryption” badge on a download page. New to VPN…

items.title: Do You Need a VPN? An Honest Answer for Each Situation
items.summary: Not for everyday browsing at home. You need one when the network you’re on shouldn’t see where you go, or blocks where you want to go. That covers fewer situations than VPN ads suggest, and a few more than the skeptics admit. Almost every site now encrypts what you send, so the old picture of a stranger reading your bank password over café Wi-Fi is mostly out of date. What’s left is quieter: the café, the hotel, your internet provider or a government can still see which sites you visit, and some of them block the ones you need. items.title: Backblaze Now Lists Purchase and Location Data Among What It Shares for Targeted Ads
items.summary: Backblaze, the cloud backup company, now says it has “sold or shared” four kinds of its customers’ personal information for targeted advertising, purchase records and location data among them. The list is in a rewritten privacy notice that takes effect on 1 December 2026. Backblaze announced it by email on 20 November; PrivacyAffairs’ editor, Miklos Zoltan, is a customer and got one.
